mime-types.quickAnswer: A MIME type (like image/png or application/json) tells browsers and servers what kind of data a file contains. Type a file extension such as pdf, mp4, or woff2 into the search box and this tool instantly shows its official MIME type and category, ready to copy into your code or server config.
keyFacts: MIME stands for Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions; the standard now covers all web content types.
A MIME type has two parts: a top-level type (text, image, audio, video, application, font) and a subtype.
Web servers send a Content-Type header with the MIME type so browsers know how to handle the file.
Serving JavaScript with the wrong MIME type can break strict module loading in modern browsers.
The +xml and +json suffixes (like image/svg+xml) mark structured syntax formats.
howTo: Type a file extension (for example, webp) or a keyword (for example, font) in the search box.
Browse the matching results showing extension, MIME type, and category.
Click the copy button on any row to copy the MIME type.
Paste it into your HTML, server config, or API headers.
Clear the search to browse the most common types.
mime-types.formula:
Extension  ->  MIME type
.pdf      ->  application/pdf
.mp4      ->  video/mp4
.woff2    ->  font/woff2
.json     ->  application/json

Searching for "pdf" returns:

Clicking copy gives you "application/pdf", which you can use in an HTTP header like:

Searching "font" lists woff, woff2, ttf, and otf with their font/* types.

faqs.a: A label like text/html or image/png that identifies the format of a file or HTTP response so software knows how to process it.

faqs.q: Why does my font fail to load with a MIME error?
faqs.a: Browsers reject fonts served with the wrong Content-Type. Serve woff2 as font/woff2 and woff as font/woff to fix it.
The generic MIME type for unknown binary data. Browsers usually download such files instead of displaying them.

faqs.q: Is there a difference between .jpg and .jpeg MIME types?
faqs.a: No. Both use image/jpeg. The two extensions are historical variants of the same format.

faqs.q: Where do I set the MIME type on my server?
faqs.a: In your server config: the mime.types file for Nginx, the staticContent section for IIS, or the AddType directive for Apache.
